etymology.historical_story: Kejar evokes pursuit, an everyday action also familiar from children's chasing games called kejar-kejar. Adding the passive prefix di- shifts attention to whoever or whatever is pursued. The image extends readily to ambition and pressure: success can be pursued, while a hurried person can feel pursued by time. The prefix itself marks voice rather than tense.

etymology.historical_story: Dakwat belongs to the Arabic-derived vocabulary associated with Malay manuscript culture. Its source is commonly connected with Arabic dawāh, an inkwell, while Malay uses the word for the liquid itself. Alongside terms for paper and pens, it recalls the materials used by scribes to copy religious works, stories, and correspondence in Jawi. See [National Library Board's manuscript exhibition guide](https://exhibitions.nlb.gov.sg/files/tmw/nlb-tmw-exh-guide_eng_e-version.pdf) and [Russell Jones's manuscript research](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/13639811.2021.1939521).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 念 dak-wat 时把 dak 收成短促的喉塞音；想象笔尖一顿，纸上落下一滴墨水。

etymology.historical_story: Dikembalikan is a transparent Malay formation rather than a separate borrowed word. Kembali supplies the idea of returning; -kan makes that return something an agent causes, and di- places the returned entity in focus. The same construction describes a borrowed book going home, money reaching its payer again, or lost rights being restored.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: kembali 是“回来”，-kan 让东西回来，di- 把镜头转向东西：dikembalikan＝被归还、被恢复。

morphology.pattern_note: 在现代马来语中作为完整词根记忆，不拆成 da- 与 haga。添加 meN- 时，词首 d 保留，形成 men-：meN- + dahaga + -i → mendahagai。

senses.nuances: 这是词典另列的 dahaga II，限于 dahaga-dahagi，不是“口渴”的比喻延伸，也不是现代日常高频用法。以下列固定形式及其解释性扩展，不冒称高频搭配。参见 [DBP：dahagi](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=dahagi)。

etymology.historical_story: Dahaga belongs to Malay's historical vocabulary of contact with South Asia. Linguist Tom Hoogervorst relates it to Middle Indo-Aryan ḍāhaga, meaning a burning sensation. The connection offers a vivid semantic bridge: a burning, dry throat becomes thirst. Modern Malay also uses this bodily experience figuratively for a strong desire for knowledge or affection. [Source: Hoogervorst](https://brill.com/display/book/9789004529458/BP000002.pdf).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 da-ha-ga 想成口干时张嘴呼出的三拍声音：“渴得直哈气”；再把身体的渴延伸成对知识的渴望。此为联想，不是词源。

morphology.formula: 输入检索形 disebalik → 规范分写 di sebalik；结构为 di + sebalik，sebalik 与 balik 同族
morphology.pattern_note: is_root 和 root_word 按输入包保留，表示该输入尚未完成词根解析，并非认定 disebalik 是语言学上的词根。这里 di 是独立介词，不是被动前缀 di-，必须分写；sebalik 的 e 读 /ə/，词尾 k 通常实现为 [ʔ]。所列 IPA 对应规范短语 di sebalik。

senses.zh_definition: 在某物背后、另一侧或被其遮挡的位置；规范写法为 di sebalik。
senses.en_definition: Behind or on the other side of something; correctly written di sebalik.
senses.ms_definition: Di sebelah belakang atau di sebelah lain sesuatu yang menjadi penghalang pandangan.
senses.nuances: 这是规范短语 di sebalik 的空间用法，不是连写 disebalik 的独立规范义项。正式记录中的 status 按要求保留为 official，但不代表连写获 DBP 认可。例句统一采用正确分写。[DBP：分写说明](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=keguruan)

senses.nuances: 常用于原因、动机、付出和幕后作用。di sebalik kejayaan 指“成功背后的因素”，不自动等于“尽管成功”；表达让步时应根据语境选用 walaupun、meskipun 或 sungguhpun。[DBP：sebalik](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=sebalik)

etymology.historical_story: The useful story is an orthographic distinction rather than the origin of a separate word. Balik includes the idea of another side, and di sebalik locates something beyond the visible surface, literally or figuratively. DBP explicitly requires a space here. The joined spelling confuses the independent preposition di with the attached passive prefix found in verbs such as ditulis. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=keguruan)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: di 问“在哪里”，sebalik 答“另一面”：想象 di 和 sebalik 之间留一道门缝，就记住必须分写。

morphology.pattern_note: 两个 e 均为 e taling /e/，不是 /ə/；词尾 k 读作喉塞音 [ʔ]。DBP 分列 derek I“行列”和 derek II“起重设备”，不可仅因同形就认定二者同源。下列派生词和复合词属于第二义项。

etymology.historical_story: Derek illustrates how a dictionary can preserve different lexical histories under one spelling. Kamus Dewan separates a word meaning a row from another referring to lifting machinery, marking the latter as Indonesian usage. That distinction matters when reading regional texts: identical letters need not carry the same meaning or geographical currency. The cited entry does not establish a shared origin. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=10456&keyword=derek)

etymology.historical_story: Dipercaya combines the passive prefix di- with percaya, the base meaning believe or trust. Its useful cultural story concerns variation across the Malay-speaking world: a familiar form in one national variety need not be the preferred editorial form in another. Malaysian dictionary examples commonly use dipercayai, making the final -i an important writing cue. See [DBP’s examples](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=244840&keyword=percaya).

etymology.historical_story: Diuruskan belongs to the Malay urus family, which includes words for affairs, managers, and management. Its structure reflects Malay grammar: di- places the handled matter in subject position, while -kan also appears in menguruskan. Administrative writing regularly uses this passive form to describe how applications, projects, and other responsibilities are handled. [Sources: DBP dictionary](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=urusan+1), [DBP administrative usage](https://dbp.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/TATA-URUSAN-KARYAWAN-TAMU.pdf).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 抓住 urus“处理”：menguruskan 是“去处理”，diuruskan 是“被处理”；看到 dah diuruskan，就想到“已经有人办好了”。

etymology.historical_story: English dev is a clipping of developer or development, rather than a word formed with Malay affixes. Its two expansions explain why a dev can be a person while a dev environment is a place for development work. In Malay technical conversation, retaining the English abbreviation creates a compact workplace expression. See [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/dev).

etymology.historical_story: Dakwa belongs to Malay’s Arabic-derived vocabulary and corresponds to Arabic daʿwā, a claim or lawsuit. Malay adds its own suffix -an to form dakwaan. The resulting noun preserves a connection between asserting something and bringing a case: a statement can be advanced in ordinary discussion or submitted for adjudication. That shared semantic background explains its courtroom and everyday meanings. [Arabic-origin Malay vocabulary study](https://oarep.usim.edu.my/server/api/core/bitstreams/b38963e9-99b5-417c-af79-7f0f570e28db/content)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 dakwa 记成“提出一套说法”，再加 -an 把动作变成内容：dakwaan＝提出的说法或指控。

etymology.historical_story: Dos brings several unrelated lexical histories together under one spelling. The medical noun denotes a measured quantity, while uppercase DOS abbreviates an English computing expression. Kamus Dewan also records a Dutch-derived homograph for a cardboard box and cardboard itself. These are separate entries meeting on the page, rather than stages in which one original meaning gradually became the others. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=dos)

etymology.historical_story: DBP records putus for broken connections and completed or settled matters. Memutuskan extends this range to cutting, terminating, determining and judicial decision. Diputuskan presents the affected matter as the grammatical focus through passive di-. The connection between ending a physical link and settling an issue offers a memory bridge, rather than a documented chronology. [DBP: putus](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=244840&keyword=putus)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: putus 是“断”；di- 是“被”；-kan 参与构成“使……断／定下来”。连接被“断开”，事项被“定下来”：diputuskan。

etymology.historical_story: Didakwa is built from dakwa and the Malay passive prefix di-. The root belongs to a family linking accusations, courtroom proceedings, and assertions of truth. That connection explains why a news report can use didakwa for a formal charge in one sentence and for an unverified allegation in another. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=dakwa)

sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 用于聘用、招生、服务和商品供应时，须区分“已提出机会”与“已接受”。传统咒术义应放在相应文化或文学语境中，不宜与现代医疗功效混同。

etymology.historical_story: Ditawarkan brings together meanings that dictionaries distinguish under tawar. In employment and commerce, it presents an offer from the recipient's side. Elsewhere, related forms concern blandness, counteracting harmful powers, or losing interest. These shared spellings should not be turned into an invented origin story: the surrounding nouns reveal which meaning is intended. [DBP: menawarkan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=menawarkan)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 di- 想成“被”：公司 menawarkan 工作，你 ditawarkan 工作；“被提供”之后还要决定是否 menerima。

morphology.pattern_note: di- 标记被动，-kan 参与构成及物动词；词根读 kəna，保持原形，不发生鼻音同化。这里的 kena 不是读 kéna、意为‘你’的古语同形词。

senses.zh_definition: 被征收费用或税款；被处以处罚；被施加规定、限制或义务。
senses.en_definition: To be charged, taxed or penalized; to have a requirement, restriction or obligation imposed.
senses.ms_definition: Dibebani bayaran, cukai atau hukuman, atau diwajibkan mematuhi sesuatu peraturan.
senses.nuances: 是 mengenakan 的被动形式。主语可以是承担者，如 pelanggan dikenakan caj，也可以是被施加的事项，如 caj dikenakan kepada pelanggan。本义不表示‘必须去做’；口语 kena bayar 的 kena 不能直接换成 dikenakan。义项依据 [DBP：kena](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=115704&keyword=kena)。

senses.ms_definition: Diarahkan supaya mengenai sasaran atau ditujukan pada sesuatu benda atau bahagian.
senses.nuances: 用于力、压力、打击等，强调有外力或施事使其作用于目标。与 terkena 相比，通常更突出施加动作，而非单纯描述意外碰到或受到影响。

senses.ms_definition: Dilekatkan, dipasang atau dikancingkan pada sesuatu.
senses.nuances: 常用于扣件、锁具等，语气偏书面或叙事。日常表达可按具体动作选用 dipasang、dikancingkan 或 dilekatkan。

collocations.en: a lock is fitted to the door

senses.zh_definition: 衣物、饰品或化妆品被穿上、戴上或施用于身体。
senses.en_definition: To be put on or worn, as clothing or jewellery, or applied as cosmetics.
senses.ms_definition: Dipakaikan pada tubuh, disarungkan pada anggota badan atau disapukan sebagai solekan.
senses.nuances: 常见于服饰报道、婚礼描写和文学叙事。以衣物为主语时可表示‘被穿着’；以佩戴动作为重点时表示‘被戴上’。日常谈穿衣更常用 dipakai。

collocations.en: a ring is placed on a finger

senses.zh_definition: 被捉弄、戏弄或用计欺骗。
senses.en_definition: To be tricked, deceived or made the target of a prank.
senses.ms_definition: Diperdaya, ditipu atau dipermainkan oleh seseorang.
senses.nuances: 多用于口语或叙事，须由人物关系和上下文判断是善意玩笑还是恶意欺骗。单独出现时也可能被理解为‘被处罚’，宜补明施事或手法。

etymology.historical_story: Dikenakan belongs to the productive Malay family of kena, associated with contact, impact and undergoing something. The dictionary connects this family with targets, fastenings, clothing, financial burdens and deception. A useful interpretation links these senses through something being brought to bear on a recipient. The prefix di- presents the action from its receiving side. [DBP: mengenakan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=wajibkan).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 抓住 kena 的‘落到身上’：费用落到你身上，就是 dikenakan caj；处罚落到你身上，就是 dikenakan hukuman。di- 提醒你从承受的一方理解。

morphology.pattern_note: 输入包误将派生词标为词根，现更正为 hubung。di- 标示被动，-i 保留；两者可分别分析，此处按字段归入 circumfix。词尾 /ŋ/ 与后缀元音组成 /ŋi/，读作 di.hu.bu.ngi。

senses.nuances: 是 menghubungi 的被动形式，本身不表示过去时；是否已经联系须看 telah、sudah 等语境。可用于人或机构。此马来文释义依据词典释义改写，并非 DBP 原文。[DBP：menghubungi](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=273844&keyword=menghubungi)

sociolinguistic_register.politeness_note: 公文、通知与客服文字常用 boleh dihubungi，语气中性而专业。正式询问可说 Bilakah pihak tuan boleh dihubungi?
sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 口语说 seseorang susah dihubungi 可能带有抱怨。向客户或上级汇报时，可用 Kami masih belum dapat menghubungi beliau，避免直接归责。

etymology.historical_story: Dihubungi belongs to the Malay family built around hubung, expressing connection and relationship. Its modern contact sense applies across letters, telephone calls and digital messages. The passive prefix di- shifts attention to the person or institution being reached. The dictionary also preserves a less familiar continuation sense, illustrating how connection can describe a response following someone's words. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=273844&keyword=menghubungi)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 记住 hubung 是“建立联系”；前面加 di-，镜头转向被联系的人：Amir dihubungi＝Amir 被联系。

etymology.historical_story: Disingkirkan is formed within Malay from singkir through the passive prefix di- and suffix -kan. Its dictionary family links moving aside with removing something or someone. That semantic connection helps explain why the same form can describe clearing an unwanted substance, dismissing an official, or knocking a team out of a tournament. [DBP: singkir](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=singkir)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: singkir 想成移到一旁；di- 表示被动：disingkirkan 就是被移开、被排除，比赛里就是被淘汰。

etymology.historical_story: Malay dekad belongs to an international vocabulary built around the idea of ten. DBP connects it with deka, also seen in dekagon, a polygon with ten sides. In accounts of national development or personal history, dekad groups passing years into manageable chapters; its Malay synonym is dasawarsa. etymology.historical_story: Depannya combines the ordinary spatial word depan with attached -nya. Its meaning depends on an established reference: a person has space in front of them, while a building has a front section. These readings grow from everyday spatial relationships. No separate historical borrowing needs to be proposed for the complete form depannya. [DBP: attached -nya](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=kamu+nya)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: depan 是“前面”，-nya 补上指代：di depannya 是“在他／它前面”，bahagian depannya 是“它的前部”。

morphology.pattern_note: 词根是 bumi，直接构词基础是 ke bumi；di-...-kan 构成被动式，整体连写，保留 /k/。主动式 meN- + (ke bumi) + -kan → mengebumikan，起首 k 被鼻音替代。输入中的整词词根标记已据 DBP 更正；缺失音节、IPA及 Jawi 按规范构形补全。参见 [DBP：mengebumikan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=mengebumikan)。

senses.ms_definition: Ditanam di dalam kubur atau dikuburkan, berkenaan dengan jenazah atau mayat; bentuk pasif bagi mengebumikan.
senses.nuances: 这是被动动词，不自带过去时：telah dikebumikan 表示已经安葬，akan dikebumikan 表示将获安葬。通常用于死者，不用于埋垃圾、种植物或电气接地。其主动词及使用范围参见 [DBP：mengebumikan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=mengebumikan)。

etymology.historical_story: Dikebumikan carries a transparent image: the deceased is placed into the earth. DBP identifies bumi as the root and ke bumi as the construction underlying the burial verb. Malay grammar then distinguishes the action, mengebumikan, from its passive, dikebumikan, and the burial process, pengebumian. The family preserves the same concrete image across different grammatical roles. [DBP: mengebumikan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=mengebumikan).

morphology.formula: di + mana + -kah → di manakah；非规范连写：dimanakah
morphology.pattern_note: 资料包中的 dimana 是连写形式，并非独立词根；核心疑问词为 mana。di 是表示处所的介词，须分写；-kah 是附着于 mana 的疑问强调小品词，不引起词干音变。

senses.zh_definition: 在哪里；用于询问人、事物或活动所处的地点。标准书面形式为 di manakah。
senses.en_definition: Where; at what place, used to ask about location. The standard written form is di manakah.
senses.ms_definition: Bentuk ejaan tidak baku bagi di manakah, iaitu ungkapan tanya untuk menanyakan tempat atau kedudukan seseorang atau sesuatu.
senses.nuances: 整体在此按处所疑问副词功能标注；马来语结构上由介词 di、疑问词 mana 和小品词 -kah 构成。正式写作使用 di manakah，日常交流常用 di mana 或 kat mana。询问目的地通常用 ke mana，询问来源用 dari mana。DBP 明确要求分写：[DBP 拼写说明](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=menyoalkan)。本条马来语释义为说明性改写，非官方逐字引文。

etymology.historical_story: This expression combines the Malay locative preposition di, the interrogative mana, and the question particle -kah. Its structure explains its spelling: di remains a separate word, while -kah attaches to mana. The joined form dimanakah obscures that boundary. DBP guidance explicitly maintains di manakah, preserving the distinction between a preposition and an attached particle.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 按三块记：di＝在，mana＝哪里，kah＝提问强调；“在｜哪里呀？”对应 di manakah，di 后留空格。

headword.status_note: official 按指定数据标签保留。现代马来西亚规范语中，表示修理或改善时通常分别采用 dibaiki 或 diperbaik；diperbaiki 另有古典文学用法。

morphology.formula: di- + per- + baik + -i → diperbaiki；现代规范对照：di- + baik + -i → dibaiki；diper- + baik → diperbaik
morphology.pattern_note: 这是派生被动形式，并非资料包所标记的独立词根。per- 中的 e 读 /ə/，baik 的 b 保留。此处 circumfix 表示包围词干的复合词缀结构，不意味着该形式可在现代规范语中自由生成。

senses.zh_definition: 被修理、修正或改善；现代常见用法，但在马来西亚规范写作中通常应依语义改用 dibaiki 或 diperbaik。
senses.en_definition: To be repaired, corrected, or improved; common in usage, but generally replaced by dibaiki or diperbaik in prescriptive Malaysian Malay.
senses.ms_definition: Dalam penggunaan umum, dibetulkan kerosakan atau kesalahannya, atau dijadikan lebih baik; bentuk baku yang disarankan ialah dibaiki atau diperbaik mengikut maksud.
senses.nuances: 修复损坏常用 dibaiki，提升质量或状况常用 diperbaik。DBP 指出，现代修理、改善义的 memperbaiki 和 diperbaiki 属于冗赘派生形式，虽有实际使用记录，规范语法仍建议改写。参见 [DBP 构词说明](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=Memperbaiki)。以下搭配记录实际用法，不作为规范写作范本。马来语释义为说明性改写。

senses.zh_definition: 受到善待或妥善对待；见于古典马来文学的被动用法。
senses.en_definition: To be treated kindly or properly, in classical literary usage.
senses.ms_definition: Dalam bahasa sastera lama, dilayan dengan baik atau diperlakukan sebagaimana yang selayaknya.
senses.nuances: 此义对应古典文学中的 memperbaiki，意思是善待某人，不能直接按现代“修理”义理解。DBP 的 memperbaiki 词条保留了这一用法：[DBP 古典词义](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=Memperbaiki)。搭配仅用于帮助理解古文。

etymology.historical_story: The root baik means good, but its derivatives preserve different meanings. DBP records classical memperbaiki as treating someone kindly, with diperbaiki as its passive counterpart. Modern speakers also use diperbaiki for repairs and improvements. Malaysian grammatical guidance distinguishes these uses, recommending dibaiki or diperbaik for modern repair and improvement contexts while retaining the classical literary sense.

etymology.historical_story: English drop has an older history than its modern campus uses: Merriam-Webster traces it through Middle English to Old English dropa. In Malaysian mixed-language conversation, context determines whether someone is discussing falling prices, withdrawing from a subject or giving a friend a lift. etymology.historical_story: Dituduh belongs to the established Malay family built on tuduh, documented by DBP alongside menuduh, tuduhan and penuduh. Its structure illustrates a central grammatical contrast: menuduh presents the accuser's action, while dituduh presents what happens to the person accused. etymology.historical_story: Diundang illustrates how Malay grammar changes perspective without replacing the central idea. Mengundang presents the person issuing an invitation; diundang presents its recipient. The same invitation image can extend figuratively to trouble that an action brings upon someone. This verbal family should be distinguished from undang-undang, the familiar expression meaning laws.

etymology.historical_story: Daily belongs to English, where its connection with day makes the central meaning transparent. In multilingual Malaysian workplaces, an English phrase such as daily report can appear inside a Malay conversation. DBP records the English word with Malay equivalents, but bilingual dictionary inclusion does not itself establish adoption as a standard Malay headword.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 读 /ˈdeɪ.li/ 时抓住 day“天”：daily 就是“每天的／每天”。换成标准马来语，修饰名词常用 harian，表示频率常用 setiap hari。

etymology.historical_story: Disayangi is a transparent Malay formation built around sayang, a word whose dictionary senses include affection, endearment, and regret. Adding di- and -i shifts attention to whoever receives the affection. Its cultural resonance reaches beyond romance: the same word family expresses parental tenderness, attachment to home, and care for others. No specific foreign origin is asserted here. [DBP entry](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=72508&keyword=sayang)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: sayang 是“疼爱”；看到 di-，把视角转向接受者：disayangi，就是“被疼爱”。

senses.zh_definition: 话题、问题或事项被提及、涉及或简略谈到。

senses.ms_definition: Disebut atau dibicarakan secara ringkas dalam ucapan, tulisan atau perbincangan.

senses.zh_definition: 感情或内心被触动；依上下文可指感动、悲伤或受到冒犯。
senses.en_definition: Of feelings or the heart, to be emotionally affected, moved, or offended.
senses.ms_definition: Dibangkitkan atau diganggu perasaannya sehingga berasa terharu, sedih atau tersinggung.
senses.nuances: 应结合 hati、perasaan 及引发情绪的事物判断褒贬。不能一律译为“感动”；日常表达自身感受时，tersentuh 或 terharu 往往更自然。马来语释义为编辑转述。[DBP 词条 sentuh](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=243192&keyword=sentuh)。

etymology.historical_story: Disentuh illustrates a transparent Malay grammatical pattern: di- places the recipient of an action in focus. Its base, sentuh, covers physical contact and extends to mentioning a subject or affecting feelings. The same conceptual movement connects touching an object, touching on an issue, and touching someone's heart. This explains the related senses without requiring a separate origin for each one. [DBP entry sentuh](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=243192&keyword=sentuh).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: di- 提醒你看“被怎样”：di- + sentuh＝被碰到；碰到身体、话题或内心，就对应三个常见义项。

etymology.historical_story: Dallas illustrates how a familiar place name can retain an uncertain naming history. The city archives report no primary evidence explaining founder John Neely Bryan’s choice. Several possible namesakes have been proposed, but none is securely established. A dictionary should therefore preserve that uncertainty rather than present one attractive story as settled fact. See the [city archives](https://dallascityhall.com/government/citysecretary/archives/Pages/Archives_DallasNameOrigin.aspx).

etymology.historical_story: Diego belongs to Iberian naming history rather than Malay word formation. The Royal Galician Academy records medieval Latin documentation under Didacus and describes the ultimate etymology as disputed. Proposed explanations include a connection with Greek vocabulary for instruction or an Iberian origin. Consequently, translating every Diego as 'teacher' or treating one proposed derivation as certain would be misleading. [Source: Royal Galician Academy](https://academia.gal/nomes/-/nome/Diego).

etymology.historical_story: Dilanggar is transparently formed within Malay from the passive prefix di- and langgar. The supplied dictionary evidence connects the root with collision, attack and crossing against an obstacle. Its abstract use makes a rule resemble a boundary that someone crosses. This offers a useful semantic connection, without claiming a documented chronology for the different meanings.

etymology.historical_story: Duluan illustrates how closely related languages can develop different conversational habits. Indonesian speakers commonly add -an to dulu when someone acts or leaves before others. Malaysian Malay generally expresses the same idea with dulu or terlebih dahulu. The supplied dictionary extract belongs to dulu, so it establishes the base word rather than official Malaysian recognition of duluan. [Indonesian usage](https://jembatanbahasa.com/first-in-indonesian/) [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=dulu)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 先记 dulu＝“先”，再把印尼口语 duluan 想成“我比别人先一步”；在马来西亚说 balik dulu 就很自然。

etymology.historical_story: Darwin enters Malay here as an English proper name rather than a native formation. Charles Darwin's scientific legacy gives the surname its familiar biological association. Australia's Darwin also commemorates him: its harbour was named in 1839, and the settlement officially adopted Darwin in 1911. These connections explain usage, without establishing the surname's deeper etymology. [Sources: Darwin Correspondence Project](https://www.darwinproject.ac.uk/about-darwin), [NT Place Names Register](https://www.ntlis.nt.gov.au/placenames/view.jsp?id=12218).

etymology.historical_story: Damien is a French form of Damian, a name connected with Greek Damianos. Oxford’s Lexicon of Greek Personal Names links Damian to the Greek root meaning “tame.” European naming traditions carried related forms across languages. In Malay, Damien functions as a person’s name, rather than as a verb meaning “to tame.” [Oxford LGPN](https://lgpn.web.ox.ac.uk/greek-names-english).

etymology.historical_story: Dilengkapi is built within Malay from lengkap, meaning complete, through the verb melengkapi and its passive counterpart. etymology.historical_story: Doraemon entered Malay usage as the name of a Japanese fictional character and his series. Shogakukan's publication records place early stories in January 1970 magazine issues. Created by Fujiko F. Fujio, the future robotic cat became the centre of a wider entertainment franchise. In Malay, the name is remembered whole rather than analysed as native affixes. [Shogakukan](https://www.shogakukan.co.jp/pr/fzenshu/lineup/doraemon/)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 do-ra-e-mon 与蓝色猫型机器人、百宝袋和大雄连成一幅画：Doraemon 就是哆啦A梦；整词记忆。

etymology.historical_story: Jatuh begins with the concrete image of falling. Its derived verb extends that image to damaged reputations, defeated governments and imposed punishments. Court language preserves a particularly useful distinction: the sentence is dijatuhkan, while the person is dijatuhi a sentence. This contrast makes an everyday image serve a precise institutional function in Malay.

etymology.historical_story: The Scottish personal name Douglas is associated with a place and river name traditionally interpreted as 'dark stream' from Gaelic elements. Douglas Heritage Museum describes a naming chain from river to village to family. This background concerns the Scottish name; it does not establish the origin of every place called Douglas. [Douglas Heritage Museum](https://douglasheritagemuseum.co.uk/douglas-the-name/)

etymology.historical_story: Dahi preserves an inherited Austronesian body-part word. The Austronesian Comparative Dictionary connects it with reconstructed *daqiS and related forms meaning forehead or face, including Iban dai. This history explains why its final -i belongs to the word itself. In Malay, the familiar forehead meaning also supports expressions about thought, appearance, and the fronts of objects. [Austronesian Comparative Dictionary](https://acd.clld.org/cognatesets/29842)

messages.zh: 我填好那张表了。他姓 Daniels，对吧？
messages.en: I've filled in the form. His surname is Daniels, right?

messages.ms_standard: Ya, ikut ejaan yang tertera dalam pasportnya sahaja.
messages.zh: 对，照他护照上的拼写写就行。
messages.en: Yes, just use the spelling in his passport.

cultural_pragmatics.usage_etiquette: 正式文件照录本人姓名拼写。缺乏上下文时，不应擅自把该形式解释为品牌、特定人物或普通马来语词。

sociolinguistic_register.politeness_note: 若确为姓氏，可按对方身份和偏好使用 Encik、Puan 或适当职衔；不能仅凭姓氏判断性别、国籍或宗教。
sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 正式文件照录本人姓名拼写。缺乏上下文时，不应擅自把该形式解释为品牌、特定人物或普通马来语词。

etymology.historical_story: As a surname, Daniels belongs to naming traditions associated with the personal name Daniel. The Dutch surname database explains Daniels or Daniëls as a patronymic with a genitive ending, historically identifying a family relationship. This documents a surname history; it does not establish what the lowercase token denotes in the supplied Malay material. [Dutch surname database](https://www.cbgfamilienamen.nl/nfb/detail_naam.php?gba_lcnaam=&info=kenmerk&kenmerk=patroniem&nfd_naam=Daniels+%28%C3%AB%29&operator=eq&taal=+target%3D_blank)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 看到 Daniels，先联想到“丹尼尔斯这个姓名”；保留结尾 s，别把它当成马来语复数或可拆词缀。

morphology.pattern_note: ny 表示单一辅音 /ɲ/，加词缀后保留；di- 是被动前缀，须与后面的词连写。di- 与 -kan 分别承担被动和派生功能，不宜视为不可分割的单一词缀。

senses.zh_definition: 被说明、注明或陈述；某项信息以口头或书面形式明确表达出来。
senses.en_definition: To be stated, specified, or explained in speech or writing.
senses.ms_definition: Diterangkan, dijelaskan atau dimaklumkan secara lisan atau bertulis.
senses.nuances: 是 menyatakan 的被动形式，常用于报告、通知和文件。dinyatakan 本身不表示过去时，也不保证所述内容属实；时间和证据须由上下文确定。马来语释义依据 [PRPM：nyata](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=72508&keyword=nyata) 的派生义改写。

senses.zh_definition: 被表达、表明；愿望、立场或感受通过言语或文字传达出来。
senses.en_definition: To be expressed or declared, especially of a wish, position, or feeling.
senses.ms_definition: Dilahirkan atau dikemukakan melalui kata-kata, khususnya tentang hasrat, pendirian atau perasaan.
senses.nuances: 主语通常是被表达的内容，如 hasrat、pendirian 或 penghargaan。日常交流常改用主动形式或 cakap 等较口语的表达，但 dinyatakan 在讨论文件内容时仍自然。

senses.zh_definition: 被显现、展示或作为证据表明。
senses.en_definition: To be manifested, displayed, or demonstrated.
senses.ms_definition: Ditampakkan, ditunjukkan atau dibuktikan melalui sesuatu tanda atau bukti.
senses.nuances: 对应 menyatakan 的“显示、表明”义，语气较书面或文学化。现代一般说明中，ditunjukkan、diperlihatkan 或 dibuktikan 往往更直接。义项依据 [PRPM：nyata](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=72508&keyword=nyata)。

dual_scenarios.zh: 该招聘广告已明确注明申请截止日期。
dual_scenarios.en: The application deadline is clearly stated in the job advertisement.

tu 是 itu 的口语缩略形式。
句末 kan 用于请求确认。
讨论书面通知时，口语可以保留 dinyatakan。

cultural_pragmatics.usage_etiquette: 适用于通知、报告、申请条件和立场表述。引用某人意见时宜注明来源；“被陈述”不等于“已证实”。

sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 适用于通知、报告、申请条件和立场表述。引用某人意见时宜注明来源；“被陈述”不等于“已证实”。

etymology.historical_story: Dinyatakan is a transparent Malay formation built on nyata, meaning clear, evident, or real. Adding -kan supports the meaning of making something clear or expressing it; di- places that action in the passive voice. The resulting word suits notices and reports because the information can occupy the foreground while the person stating it remains unnamed. This is productive morphology rather than a separate borrowed word. [Source: PRPM](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=72508&keyword=nyata).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: nyata＝清楚；nyata + -kan＝说清楚；前面加 di-，就变成“被说清楚、被注明”。

morphology.pattern_note: di- 是被动前缀，连写于 uji 前，不表示地点，也不标记过去时；相邻元音通常分属不同音节。将输入中的词根标记修正为 uji。Jawi 按 di- 接元音起首词根的规则补写。[DBP：uji 词族](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=Alat+uji)

word_family.gloss: 经过检验的；经受过考验的

senses.zh_definition: 被测试、检验或试验，以确定性质、质量、功能或真实状况。
senses.en_definition: To be tested or examined to establish quality, properties, performance or condition.
senses.ms_definition: Diperiksa atau dicuba untuk mengetahui mutu, sifat, fungsi atau keadaan sebenarnya.
senses.nuances: 是 menguji 的被动形式。diuji 本身不表示已经完成：akan diuji 是“将被测试”，sedang diuji 是“正在测试”，telah diuji 是“已经测试”；受测也不等于通过测试。

collocations.zh: 接受测试以确认安全性

senses.zh_definition: 接受能力、知识、技巧或表现方面的测验或考核。
senses.en_definition: To be assessed for knowledge, skill or ability.
senses.ms_definition: Dinilai atau diperiksa untuk mengetahui tahap pengetahuan, kepandaian atau kecekapan.
senses.nuances: 主语可以是考生，也可以是被考查的能力。说明考查范围可用 diuji dalam；说明考核方式可用 diuji melalui。

senses.zh_definition: 经受考验；人的耐心、忠诚、毅力或处境受到困难的挑战。
senses.en_definition: To be put to the test by difficulty, temptation or adversity.
senses.ms_definition: Diduga atau dicuba ketabahan, kesabaran, kesetiaan atau keteguhannya melalui sesuatu keadaan.
senses.nuances: 可用于世俗或宗教语境。diuji dengan musibah 表示遭遇不幸、经受考验；只有上下文明确提及信仰时，才应译出神意。[DBP：uji、menguji 与 ujian](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=Alat+uji)

kat 在此对应地点介词 di
okey je 表示“都正常，没什么问题”

etymology.historical_story: The root uji connects modern testing with the concrete practice of checking gold using a batu uji, or touchstone, a sense retained in Malay dictionaries. Diuji places the tested object or person in focus. From material quality, the word’s uses extend to knowledge, loyalty and patience under pressure.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 di- 记成“被”，uji 记成“测试”：diuji＝被测试、受考验；要表达“已经”，还需看 dah、sudah 或 telah。

morphology.formula: di + (dalam + -nya) → di dalamnya；didalamnya 为非规范连写
morphology.pattern_note: root_word 按输入保留 didalam，但规范分析的基础词是 dalam。di 是独立介词，不是被动前缀 di-；-nya 是附着成分，接在 dalam 后，/m/ 保留，ny 读 /ɲ/。suffix 为本模式对词尾附着成分的近似归类。

senses.zh_definition: 规范短语 di dalamnya 的非规范连写，表示“在其里面；在其中”，通常回指前文提到的容器或有内部空间的处所。
senses.en_definition: A nonstandard joined spelling of di dalamnya, meaning inside it or within it.
senses.ms_definition: Ejaan tidak baku bagi frasa di dalamnya, yang bermaksud di bahagian dalam sesuatu tempat atau bekas yang telah disebut.
senses.nuances: 这里的 pos 表示整个介词短语的功能，并不表示 didalamnya 是规范的单个介词。规范拼写必须分开 di 与 dalamnya；-nya 仍连写。抽象领域通常用 dalam，例如 dalam perkara itu，不宜机械套用 di dalam。所有教学例句采用规范拼写。马来语释义为编辑说明。依据：[DBP 马来语拼写指南](https://eseminar.dbp.gov.my/dokumen/ejaan.pdf)、[DBP：dalam 与 di dalam](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=dalam+di+dalam)。

dulu 在这里对应较正式的 dahulu。

di dalamnya 在口语中仍可使用，也常换成 kat dalam；口语不改变其规范分词规则。

etymology.historical_story: This form illustrates a spelling distinction rather than a separate word origin. Malay writes the locative preposition di separately from the following expression, while the attached element -nya stays joined to the preceding word. The standard result is di dalamnya. Writing all three components together obscures that grammatical structure. Source: [DBP spelling guidelines](https://eseminar.dbp.gov.my/dokumen/ejaan.pdf).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: di 像站在门外的定位牌，要留空格；-nya 像贴在 dalam 身上的标签，要连写：di | dalamnya＝在它里面。

morphology.pattern_note: di- 构成被动动词，词根开头的 t 保留；与主动式 meN- + tukar → menukar 的 t 脱落不同。输入包将 ditukar 判作词根有误，此处按实际构词修正。

etymology.historical_story: Ditukar is transparently formed within Malay: tukar supplies the idea of changing or exchanging, while di- places the affected thing in focus. The same root connects everyday replacement, currency exchange, and staff transfers. This shared vocabulary makes a shop counter and an administrative office surprisingly close linguistic neighbours, without requiring a separate borrowed verb for each activity.

etymology.historical_story: Derma belongs to Malay's Sanskrit-derived vocabulary. An early Malay language manual connects it with dharma and translates its Malay meaning as charity or benevolence. The connection is memorable: a term associated with duty and moral conduct became established in Malay as a word for a generous gift to others. [Historical language manual](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/6c/A_manual_of_the_Malay_language._With_an_introductory_sketch_of_the_Sanskrit_element_in_Malay_%28IA_manualofmalaylan00maxwrich%29.pdf).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: derma 可联想“德”：把善意化成捐助。再串记 derma 捐款 → menderma 捐赠 → penderma 捐赠者。

etymology.historical_story: In wayang kulit, the dalang moves the figures while telling their story. This cultural role offers a vivid way to understand the figurative meaning: someone unseen directs what others do. etymology.historical_story: Dibelasah combines the productive Malay passive prefix di- with belasah, a root associated with forceful beating. Dictionaries also record a figurative extension to overwhelming defeat. The connection is easy to visualize: a team suffering a heavy loss is described as though it has taken a beating. This explains the meaning without inventing an older origin. [DBP: belasah](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=belasah)

etymology.historical_story: The supplied packet provides no definition, pronunciation, or historical evidence for darhk. DC does attest Damien Darhk as a fictional character's name, making a proper-name interpretation possible. That attestation does not establish the intended reference here or explain the spelling's origin. A responsible entry preserves the uncertainty rather than inventing a Malay ancestry.

senses.zh_definition: 被听见；声音、话语或音乐被耳朵感知。
senses.en_definition: To be heard or perceived by the ear.
senses.ms_definition: Ditangkap atau diterima oleh telinga, berkenaan bunyi, suara dan sebagainya.

etymology.historical_story: Didengar belongs to the Malay dengar family. The passive prefix di- shifts attention from the listener to the sound, story, or opinion received. Its uses connect hearing with social attention: a voice may reach the ear, while advice may receive consideration. The dictionary preserves both meanings within this productive family. [Source: DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=dengar)

etymology.historical_story: Disumpah is transparently formed from the passive prefix di- and sumpah. The root covers both solemn oaths and curses, making context essential. Malay storytelling supplies a vivid example: the dictionary invokes Si Tenggang, who turns to stone after his mother's curse. The passive form places the person receiving the curse at the centre. [DBP: sumpah](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=72508&keyword=sumpah)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 记住 di- 把镜头转向承受者：menyumpah 是“咒骂别人”，disumpah 是“被别人咒骂”。

morphology.formula: digital video disc → DVD；∅ + DVD → DVD

senses.ms_definition: Kependekan digital video disc: cakera video digital, iaitu cakera yang boleh menyimpan filem atau muzik yang lebih banyak dan lebih berkualiti berbanding dengan cakera padat.
senses.nuances: DBP 词条以 digital video disc 释名，术语库亦列 digital versatile disc，对应 cakera serba boleh digital。DVD 本身指光盘或格式；播放设备须说 pemain DVD。光盘格式本身不保证所有内容都有更高画质。[PRPM：DVD](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=371752&keyword=dvd)。

etymology.historical_story: DVD entered Malay as an international initialism rather than through Malay affixation. DBP records digital video disc, while its terminology database also recognizes digital versatile disc. The two expansions reflect the medium’s association with films and its broader storage uses. Malay places the borrowed label after local nouns in expressions such as pemain DVD. [Source: PRPM](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=371752&keyword=dvd).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 按字母念 di-vi-di；把 V 联想成 video，再把整词连到“一张装影片的数字光盘”。

etymology.historical_story: Dit urunkan is not a separate historical root: written correctly as diturunkan, it combines passive di-, turun and -kan. Its dictionary meanings span physical lowering, inheritance, revelation and written transmission. A downward image offers a useful learning connection, although it should not be treated as proof of each meaning’s historical development. Reference: [DBP](https://ekamus.dbp.gov.my/Search.aspx?cari=turun&type=1).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: turun 是下；-kan 使它下；di- 换成被动：diturunkan，就是被降下、被调低或被传下。

etymology.historical_story: The root isi names what is inside something: its contents, substance, or a fruit's flesh. Malay builds mengisi for putting contents in, and diisi for presenting the receiving object as the subject. The same image extends naturally from bottles to forms, vacant jobs, and free time. These meanings share a transparent construction rather than separate origins.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: isi＝内容；di-＝被：diisi＝被填入内容。两个 i 都保留，记作 di｜isi。

etymology.historical_story: Deria belongs to the Sanskrit-derived vocabulary of Malay. Satya Vrat Shastri records it as a variant of enderia and connects the word with Sanskrit indriya, meaning a sense organ or sensory faculty. Its modern use in discussions of sight, hearing, and smell preserves that central association with perception. [Source: Shastri, Sanskrit Words in Southeast Asian Languages](https://www.wisdomlib.org/history/book/sanskrit-words-in-southeast-asian-languages/d/doc1595639.html).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 deria 和「感官雷达」一起记：眼看、耳听、鼻闻，都是 deria 接收的信号；这是联想，不是词源拆分。

etymology.historical_story: The noun dunia comes from Arabic dunya, a source connection discussed by Malaysia's Institute of Islamic Understanding. Its association with present earthly life remains visible when paired with akhirat, the hereafter. In di dunia, however, di is simply a separate Malay preposition. The joined spelling didunia does not establish a new root or a separate historical word. Source: [IKIM](https://www.ikim.gov.my/the-world-of-nature-as-alam-and-as-dunya/).

etymology.historical_story: English dance descends from Middle English dauncen, borrowed from Anglo-French dancer, with English evidence dating to the fourteenth century. That history belongs to the English word; it does not establish an official Malay borrowing. For Malay learners, the practical distinction is between English dance and the established Malay expressions menari and tarian. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/dance)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 听到 dance，就想“跟着节拍动起来”；动作对应 menari，舞蹈对应 tarian。不要按马来语拼读成 dan.ce。

etymology.historical_story: Kamus Dewan preserves dol as an archaic drum name, but its brief definition does not identify a donor language or borrowing date. The same spelling also survives in separate entries for a ship’s mast and a loose fastening. This illustrates how identical word forms can conceal different histories; a shared origin should not be assumed. [DBP PRPM](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=371752&keyword=dol)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 鼓义可联想低沉的一声“咚”：dol，敲鼓响。这只是声音联想，不是词源解释；遇到 kapal 或 skru，要分别转向船桅义或松动义。

etymology.historical_story: Dikirim combines the Malay passive prefix di- with kirim. The dictionary records kirim with letters, greetings, money, and dispatched groups, showing how one sending concept connects personal relationships and organized activity. Modern communication extends that familiar pattern to electronic messages. This account describes documented usage; it does not establish a deeper historical origin for kirim. [DBP: kirim](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=10456&keyword=kirim)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 kirim 想成“寄”；前面加 di-，视角转向物品：信件“被寄送”。di- 表被动，不等于“已经”。

morphology.pattern_note: di- 标记被动，-kan 构成使对象分离的及物动词；词根首音 p 保留。此处 di- 与动词连写。affix_type 依给定分类记作 circumfix，具体成分为前缀 di- 与后缀 -kan。

senses.zh_definition: 被分开、隔开或分离；原本相连、相处或混合的人或物被置于彼此分开的状态。
senses.en_definition: To be separated, divided, or kept apart from another person or thing.
senses.ms_definition: Dijadikan berasingan atau tidak lagi bersama, bercantum atau bercampur dengan pihak atau benda yang lain.
senses.nuances: 是 memisahkan 的被动形式，突出承受分离的人或物。按所指关系使用 dipisahkan daripada、dipisahkan oleh 或 dipisahkan kepada。与 terpisah 相比，更突出分离这一动作及其施事或原因。[DBP：pisah 及其派生词](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=10456&keyword=pisah)。

collocations.zh: 被迫或被安排与家人分开

senses.zh_definition: 在概念、分析或制度上被区分、划开或分别处理。

senses.ms_definition: Dibezakan atau diasingkan dari segi konsep, analisis atau pengurusan.
senses.nuances: 常用于事实与意见、职责与利益、相互关联的议题。不可分割的关系常用 tidak dapat dipisahkan 表达。此处是依据词根释义及被动构词形成的释义，并非独立 DBP 原文。

senses.zh_definition: 群体或原有整体被拆散，形成彼此分离的部分。
senses.en_definition: For a group or whole to be broken up into separate parts.
senses.ms_definition: Sesuatu kumpulan atau keseluruhan dipecahkan sehingga bahagiannya tidak lagi bersatu.
senses.nuances: 强调整体或群体被拆开的结果；语气可中性，也可表达对人际分离或社会分裂的负面评价。不要把所有 dipisahkan 都理解为婚姻关系解除。

etymology.historical_story: Dipisahkan illustrates productive Malay word formation rather than a separate borrowed word. The root pisah supplies the idea of separation; -kan forms the transitive base, and di- presents the event from the affected participant’s perspective. Its active counterpart is memisahkan. This explains the modern structure without making an unsupported claim about the root’s earliest historical origin.

etymology.historical_story: English demon ultimately comes from Greek daimōn through Latin daemon. The Greek word could refer to a divine power or guiding spirit without necessarily implying evil. Later religious usage strengthened the hostile supernatural meaning familiar today. That change explains why historical discussions may distinguish daimon from demon, even though the words share an origin. [Etymological reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/daimon)

etymology.historical_story: English doctor ultimately comes from Latin doctor, meaning a teacher, related to docere, to teach. Its academic associations help explain why the title can identify a scholar as well as a medical practitioner. Malay uses the established spelling doktor for these roles. This shared history does not make the English spelling a standard Malay headword. See [doctor etymology](https://www.etymonline.com/word/doctor).

etymology.historical_story: Dimaafkan combines the Arabic-derived word maaf with Malay grammatical elements. The borrowed vocabulary supplies the idea of pardon, while di- marks the passive and -kan belongs to the verb formation. This illustrates how a loanword becomes part of a productive Malay family, connecting everyday apologies with expressions of forgiveness and a forgiving character. [阿拉伯语借词研究](https://langsci-press.org/catalog/view/78/35/613-3.pdf), [DBP maaf](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=maaf)。

etymology.historical_story: English door continues Old English duru and dor, words for a door or gate. Its history belongs to English, rather than to a demonstrated Malay borrowing. This distinction matters in a multilingual lexicon: an English word appearing in Malaysian material does not automatically become a standard Malay headword. The established Malay equivalent here is pintu. [Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/door)

etymology.historical_story: Dirasuk belongs to the rasuk family associated with possession and deep influence. Malay dictionaries distinguish this rasuk from its homonym meaning a house beam. In stories, something enters and takes control; figuratively, anger or desire can occupy the same role. The passive prefix di- shifts attention to the person experiencing that overwhelming influence. [DBP: rasuk II](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=274404&keyword=rasuk)

etymology.historical_story: Did belongs to English rather than the verified Malay vocabulary supplied here. Its relationship with do illustrates an irregular English past form. In a Malay conversation about an English exercise, did can appear as the word being discussed; that appearance alone does not establish it as a Malay borrowing. [Cambridge](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/did)

senses.zh_definition: 被画出、描绘或以视觉形象表现。
senses.en_definition: To be drawn, depicted, or represented visually.
senses.ms_definition: Dilukis atau dipaparkan dalam bentuk gambar.

senses.zh_definition: 被描述、叙述或塑造成某种形象；通过文字、影像等得到呈现。

etymology.historical_story: Gambar provides the concrete image behind this word: a picture becomes something that can portray a person, a scene, or an idea. Malay builds menggambarkan for the active action and digambarkan for its passive counterpart. The dictionary meanings bridge actual drawing, verbal portrayal, and mental imagery, giving one word several connected uses. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=243192&keyword=menggambarkan)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: gambar＝图像；看见 di- 就把镜头转向被描绘的对象：digambarkan＝被画出来、被描述出来。

etymology.historical_story: The dictionary records taruh and its family across placing, keeping, wagering, and entrusting. These meanings share a useful image: something valuable is placed in someone else's hands or exposed to an outcome. Dipertaruhkan is the passive counterpart of mempertaruhkan. This semantic connection explains the modern range without claiming a documented chronological sequence. [DBP dictionary](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=taruh+kan)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: taruh 想成“放上去”：把钱、名声或生命放上赌桌；di- 提醒你，主语是“被押上”的对象。

etymology.historical_story: Dramatik belongs to the international vocabulary associated with drama and theatrical expression. In Malay, its dictionary meanings connect a style suited to performance with the emotional impression a story or event creates. That connection offers a useful cultural bridge from the stage to everyday description. The supplied evidence does not establish the exact borrowing route.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 dramatik 和 drama 连起来：像舞台戏剧一样有表现力，或让人情绪强烈起伏。

etymology.historical_story: This word illustrates Malay word formation rather than a separate borrowed origin. Ingin expresses desire; menginginkan directs that desire towards something; diinginkan presents that thing as desired. DBP also uses diinginkan when defining keinginan. The related forms show how Malay builds a connected vocabulary of wishes, wanting, and wanted outcomes. See [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=keinginan).

etymology.historical_story: The useful story here is Malay word formation: hasil names an outcome or yield, while menghasilkan presents the act of producing one. Dihasilkan changes the viewpoint so that the product or outcome becomes the focus. The same root therefore connects factory output, creative work, and the effects of an activity. [DBP: hasil](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=399108&keyword=hasil%20).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: hasil＝成果；di-...-kan 把镜头转向成果：dihasilkan＝“被做出来、被产生”。

sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 常用于考试、面试、患病、出行和人生大事。面对不同信仰的听者，应尊重对方是否愿意参与祈祷；单纯表达祝愿也可说Semoga semuanya berjalan lancar。

etymology.historical_story: Doakan combines doa, from Arabic duʿāʾ, meaning supplication, with the Malay suffix -kan. The formation makes prayer something directed toward another person's welfare or a hoped-for outcome. This explains the warmth of Doakan saya before an examination, interview, or operation: the speaker is asking another person to remember them in prayer. The full active form is mendoakan. [DBP: mendoakan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=mendoakan).

senses.ms_definition: Berpantang atau mengehadkan makanan tertentu; berdiet.

etymology.historical_story: The international word diet ultimately belongs to a Greek word family concerning a way of living. Through Latin and French, English inherited a term that gradually focused on food and regulated eating. Malay uses diet for both ordinary nourishment and planned eating, preserving a useful distinction that everyday talk about slimming can obscure. See [American Heritage](https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=diet).

etymology.historical_story: The base maklum belongs to Malay vocabulary associated with knowing and being informed. Malay morphology builds memaklumkan for communicating information and dimaklumkan for its passive counterpart. In administrative writing, the latter introduces notices while allowing the sender to remain implicit. This explains its familiar institutional tone without treating the entire four-syllable form as an indivisible root. See [PRPM: maklum](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=371752&keyword=maklum).

etymology.historical_story: Khianat belongs to Malay's Arabic-derived vocabulary of trust and moral conduct. Malay grammar builds on that borrowed base: mengkhianati presents the betrayer's action, while dikhianati places the injured party in focus. The word therefore travels naturally between personal relationships and public discussions of responsibility, carrying a stronger moral judgement than ordinary disappointment.

etymology.historical_story: Dilantik is transparently formed from lantik with the Malay passive prefix di-. Kamus Dewan illustrates the word family with appointments to public office and Tun Perak's appointment as Bendahara, linking present administrative language with Malay political history. The passive form places the appointee first, making it especially useful in appointment letters and news announcements. [DBP: lantik](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=lantik)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 听到 di-lantik，就在脑中给某人戴上任命名牌：di- 表示“被”，lantik 表示“任命”，合起来就是“被任命”。

etymology.historical_story: There is no separate word history to assign to disekitar: it is a joined spelling of di sekitar. The useful background is Malay's distinction between the independent location preposition di and the attached passive prefix di-. Recognising that contrast explains why a place expression needs a space, while a passive verb such as ditulis does not.

etymology.historical_story: The root seksa is traced to Sanskrit śikṣā, associated with instruction, discipline, and chastisement. Malay developed a strong association with punishment and suffering. Adding the productive passive prefix di- places the sufferer at the centre of the sentence. The resulting form appears in accounts of cruelty and in descriptions of emotional torment. [Etymological reference](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/seksa).

etymology.historical_story: Dominic comes from Latin dominicus, meaning belonging to the Lord. The name was originally associated with children born on Sunday, the Lord’s day. It later spread through devotion to Saint Dominic, founder of the Dominican Order. This history explains the name’s Christian associations, but a modern bearer’s name alone does not establish their religion. [Dictionary of Medieval Names from European Sources](https://dmnes.org/name/Dominic)

etymology.historical_story: DJ abbreviates the English expression disc jockey. The expression preserves the association with recorded discs, while Malay dictionary usage covers people presenting and playing music on radio or at entertainment venues. Learners should remember the occupation as a whole: its duties may include talking to listeners as well as selecting music. [Source](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=dj).

etymology.historical_story: This entry illustrates a boundary between languages rather than a Malay derivation. DBP records dent in its English–Malay dictionary and distinguishes a hollow in a general surface from damage to metal. The same physical image also supports English figurative uses involving confidence or reputation. Its appearance in Malaysian conversation does not establish a standard Malay headword.

etymology.historical_story: Harga belongs to Malay's Sanskrit loanword heritage, deriving from argha, meaning value or price. In modern Malay, the family spans both monetary valuation and appreciation of people. Dihargai is the passive form: someone's contribution, advice, or presence receives recognition. The connection between price and appreciation provides a useful semantic bridge. [Source: Maxwell's Malay manual](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/25604/pg25604-images.html).

etymology.historical_story: Lulus has dictionary senses involving passage through an opening, success in examinations, and approval of requests. These meanings invite a useful image: something gets through a barrier. This is a semantic comparison, not a documented chronology. Diluluskan applies Malay passive morphology, placing the application, proposal, or candidate at the centre of the statement. [Source: DBP lulus](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=72508&keyword=lulus).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 lulus 想成“过关”：di-lulus-kan，就是“被准许过关”——获批、获通过。

morphology.formula: di- + lancar + -kan → dilancarkan（被启动／被发射／被使之顺畅）
morphology.pattern_note: di- 标示被动，-kan 参与构成及物动词；词根不变，c 读 /tʃ/。这是 melancarkan 的被动形式；输入包将其标作词根，现按构词关系更正为 lancar。

senses.zh_definition: 被启动、推出或正式发布，指活动、计划、产品或出版物开始实施或首次面向公众。
senses.en_definition: To be launched, initiated, or introduced to the public, of an activity, programme, product, or publication.
senses.ms_definition: Dimulakan, bagi sesuatu kegiatan atau rancangan, atau diperkenalkan kepada masyarakat buat kali pertama, bagi produk atau terbitan.
senses.nuances: 常见于 kempen、program、produk 和 buku 等主语之后。dilancarkan 本身不表示过去时，时间由 telah、akan 或上下文确定。此义与以下各义依据 melancarkan 的词典释义转写为被动形式。[DBP：melancarkan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=228452&keyword=melancarkan)

senses.zh_definition: 被发射或送出，指火箭、卫星、导弹等被推动进入预定运行路径。
senses.en_definition: To be launched or propelled into flight or a trajectory, of a rocket, satellite, missile, or similar object.
senses.ms_definition: Digerakkan atau diluncurkan dengan cepat ke udara, angkasa atau arah tertentu.
senses.nuances: 侧重实际发射动作。卫星被发射不等于已经成功进入轨道，后者通常另用 berjaya memasuki orbit 表达。

collocations.en: a satellite is launched into space

senses.zh_definition: 被发动或展开，指攻击、攻势或有组织的行动开始实施。
senses.en_definition: To be launched or carried out, of an attack, offensive, or organised action.
senses.ms_definition: Dilakukan atau diadakan, khususnya serangan, tindakan atau gerakan.
senses.nuances: serangan dilancarkan 强调攻击被发动；不能据此推断攻击已经成功。也可用于批评攻势等比喻语境。

senses.zh_definition: 被使之更加顺畅、通畅或高效，指流程、事务或沟通中的阻碍得到减少。
senses.en_definition: To be made to proceed smoothly or efficiently; to be facilitated.
senses.ms_definition: Dijadikan lancar atau dilicinkan supaya sesuatu urusan, pergerakan atau usaha berjalan dengan baik.
senses.nuances: 此义强调改善运行状态，区别于首次启动。现代行文中 diperlancar 或 diperlancarkan 也常用于明确表达“使更顺畅”。

etymology.historical_story: DBP records lancar for smooth movement and fluent speech, alongside melancarkan for launching spacecraft, starting campaigns, and facilitating work. These related meanings offer a useful semantic picture: something moves forward or begins operating. Dilancarkan adds passive grammar to that family, placing the launched object or activity at the centre of attention. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=lancar)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: lancar＝顺畅向前；-kan＝使之如此；di-＝被：dilancarkan 就是“被推动起来”，进而记住“被启动／被发射”。

headword.data_note: 科学单位 darcy 的身份可以核实，但数据包不足以确定原始语料采用单位义还是专名 Darcy，也不足以认定其为 DBP 核定词条。以下列出两种候选解释；未指定马来语规范读音或爪夷文。

morphology.formula: ∅ + darcy → darcy（单位名）；∅ + Darcy → Darcy（专名）
morphology.pattern_note: 按数据包保留未派生分析，不表示该形式属于马来语本源词。单位名与专名须按语境区分；milli- 等为国际科学构词成分，不是马来语本土词缀。

word_family.gloss: 微达西；百万分之一达西

senses.zh_definition: 【科学；候选义】达西，多孔介质固有渗透率的非国际单位制单位；1 达西约等于 9.86923 × 10⁻¹³ 平方米。
senses.en_definition: A non-SI unit of intrinsic permeability, approximately equal to 9.86923 × 10⁻¹³ square metres.
senses.ms_definition: Unit bukan SI bagi ketelapan intrinsik medium berliang, dengan satu darcy bersamaan kira-kira 9.86923 × 10⁻¹³ meter persegi.
senses.nuances: 用于地质、石油工程和多孔介质流动讨论，不能与量纲为长度除以时间的水力传导系数混同。此马来语释义为依据技术资料编写，并非 DBP 引文。单位定义、换算及相关单位依据：[API《岩心分析推荐规程》第 6.1.2 节](https://energistics.org/sites/default/files/2022-10/rp40.pdf)。以下搭配为技术用法示例，未据语料统计其频率。

collocations.zh: 以达西为单位的渗透率

senses.zh_definition: 【专名；候选义】Darcy，姓氏或人名；具体所指须由原文确定，不能由小写输入直接认定。
senses.en_definition: Darcy, a surname or personal name whose referent must be established from context.
senses.ms_definition: Darcy ialah nama khas bagi seseorang; identiti orang yang dimaksudkan perlu ditentukan daripada konteks.
senses.nuances: noun 在此包含专名。用于人名时通常首字母大写；不把所有 Darcy 都理解为科学家 Henry Darcy，也不把人名本身定义为渗透率单位。Henry Darcy 与单位名称的关系见：[USGS 渗透率资料](https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1982/0166/report.pdf)。以下组合为特定人物的称名及相关术语，不是一般人名的高频搭配。

sociolinguistic_register.politeness_note: 讨论专业资料时，先解释单位并明确换算关系；向非专业听众介绍时可补充 unit ketelapan，避免仅报一个陌生术语。

etymology.historical_story: The permeability unit darcy commemorates Henry Darcy, whose work established a foundational relationship for flow through porous materials. Petroleum and groundwater specialists use the name when discussing how readily fluids pass through a medium. That scientific history explains the unit, but it cannot establish whether this contextless corpus token denotes the unit or a person.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 单位义可想象“达西让水穿过砂石”：记住它衡量介质的渗透率；专名 Darcy 则先认作人名，再查具体人物。

morphology.pattern_note: 外来词整词作为独立词素记忆，不拆成 do- 与 -nat；词尾 /t/ 常不完全释放。以下是食品名称组合，没有派生词缀。

senses.zh_definition: 甜甜圈；通常以小麦粉、酵母等制成并油炸的甜点，典型形状为圆环，常裹糖或加糖霜。

senses.ms_definition: Sejenis kuih berbentuk gelang yang dibuat daripada tepung gandum, yis dan bahan lain, digoreng serta disalut dengan gula halus.
senses.nuances: 词典描述以环形裹糖款为典型；现代面包店也用 donat 指夹馅或没有中央孔洞的款式。donat 是甜点名称，不表示捐款，也不等同于所有马来传统油炸糕点。

etymology.historical_story: Donat is a Malay adaptation of English donut, a spelling variant of doughnut. The borrowed name became an ordinary Malay food word, while the spelling reflects its local pronunciation. The supplied Dewan definition compares the pastry with kuih keria, offering a familiar culinary reference without claiming that the two foods share the same ingredients or historical origin. [Etymology reference](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/donat#Malay)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把英语 donut 与马来语 do.nat 配成一对，脑中放一个圆环甜点；记住末尾写 -nat。

morphology.pattern_note: di- 构成被动式，与词根连写；词根 usir 不变，i 与 u 分属相邻音节。输入包将 diusir 判为词根有误，此处按实际构词修正。

senses.zh_definition: 被驱逐；被强行赶离某个地方、住所或群体。

senses.ms_definition: Disuruh pergi dengan paksa; dihalau dari sesuatu tempat.
senses.nuances: 是 mengusir 的被动式，主语为被赶走的人或动物；通常带有强制、排斥或敌意，不等于一般的离开，也不自动表示依法遣返。词义依据：[DBP PRPM：usir 词族](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1.aspx?d=73980&keyword=pengusir)。

senses.ms_definition: Dikejar atau diburu, khususnya dalam penggunaan sastera lama.
senses.nuances: 承接 usir 在旧文献中的“追赶、追捕”义。以下为帮助阅读古典语境而构造的搭配，不作为现代高频表达；现代通常用 dikejar 或 diburu。[DBP PRPM：usir 词族](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1.aspx?d=73980&keyword=pengusir)。

etymology.historical_story: Malay dictionaries preserve two meanings of usir: pursuing someone and forcing someone away. This makes older stories potentially surprising: a person described as diusir may be chased rather than expelled. The prefix di- places the affected participant in focus. Modern everyday interpretation usually favours expulsion, while surrounding events help readers recover the older pursuit meaning. etymology.historical_story: The English name daisy descends from an Old English expression meaning day's eye. Its image comes from the flower opening in the morning and closing at night, like an eye responding to daylight. Malay records the adapted spelling daisi. Remembering that small daily movement connects the borrowed flower name with an observable feature rather than an invented Malay affix. [Oxford](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/daisy_1); [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=daisi)

etymology.historical_story: Ditunjukkan belongs to the Malay tunjuk family, built around showing and indicating. Its structure illustrates how Malay grammar shifts attention: menunjukkan foregrounds someone showing something, while ditunjukkan foregrounds what is shown. The doubled k preserves the meeting point between tunjuk and -kan. DBP explicitly identifies di-...-kan in this word as passive morphology. [DBP: grammatical guidance](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=tunjuk+kan)

etymology.historical_story: Ditendang is transparently formed from di-, the Malay passive prefix, and tendang, kick. Its story also illustrates a familiar semantic extension: physical kicking becomes social removal. Kamus Dewan records the corresponding active verb for both striking with the foot and colloquially expelling or dismissing someone. The passive preserves these meanings while foregrounding whoever or whatever receives the action. See [DBP: tendang](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=tendang).

etymology.historical_story: Dikepung is transparently formed within Malay from kepung and the passive prefix di-. Kamus Dewan illustrates this family with a passage about Bugis forces surrounding a fort, placing the word in the language of historical warfare. Modern police reporting retains the same spatial image: a person or place enclosed by forces positioned around it. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=kepung)

morphology.pattern_note: 规范拼写为 di sinilah。di 是独立的处所介词，须与 sini 分写；-lah 是附着于 sini 的强调小品词，不引起词干音变。输入词根 disini 对应规范形式 di sini，核心指示词为 sini。

senses.zh_definition: 就在这里；正是在这个地方。强调某人或某事所在、发生的具体位置。
senses.en_definition: Right here; at this very place, with emphasis on the location.
senses.ms_definition: Di tempat ini, dengan penegasan pada tempat seseorang atau sesuatu berada atau sesuatu peristiwa berlaku.
senses.nuances: 输入形式 disinilah 属于不规范连写，正式书面语应写 di sinilah。整体是具有处所副词功能的介词短语；-lah 强调位置，并不自动表示命令。其基本处所义依据 [DBP《Kamus Dewan》sini 词条](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=259120&keyword=sini)；强调功能参见 [DBP 关于 di sini／di sinilah 的说明](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=sinilah)。

etymology.historical_story: The expression combines the place marker di, the demonstrative sini, and the emphatic particle -lah. Its cultural appeal lies in turning a simple location into a focal point: a storyteller can identify where everything began, while a speaker can identify where a problem lies. These uses connect physical place with rhetorical emphasis. Modern standard spelling keeps di separate and attaches -lah to sini.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 三步定位：di＝在，sini＝这里，-lah＝强调；连起来就是“就在这里！”记得写成 di sinilah。

morphology.formula: dapat + -nya → dapatnya（具体意义由 -nya 的句法功能决定）
morphology.pattern_note: 词根不发生音变；ny 表示单一辅音 /ɲ/，分音为 da.pat.nya。-nya 在这里可作附着代词或名词化成分，不能一律当作普通派生后缀。headword.jawi 按输入保留 داڤت，但该拼写只对应 dapat；带 -nya 的完整形式应为 داڤتڽ。

senses.zh_definition: 得到它、取得那个东西；口语中由表示获得的 dapat 与回指已知对象的 -nya 组合而成。
senses.en_definition: To get or obtain it, with -nya referring to an understood object in colloquial usage.
senses.ms_definition: Memperoleh atau menerima sesuatu yang telah disebut atau difahami daripada konteks, dengan -nya merujuk kepada perkara tersebut.
senses.nuances: 这是按构词和语境解释的形式，并非输入所附 dapat 词条的独立释义。表示获得的裸词根 dapat 本身具有口语用法；正式表达通常改用 mendapatkannya 或明确说出宾语。不能把 dapatnya 一概译成“他能”。[PRPM：dapat](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=274052&keyword=dapat)

senses.zh_definition: 能否办到、是否能够实现；在 dapat tidaknya 等结构中，-nya 使表示能力或可能性的表达名词化。
senses.en_definition: The possibility or feasibility of doing something, especially in constructions meaning whether something can be done.
senses.ms_definition: Hal dapat atau tidak dapat sesuatu dilakukan atau dicapai, khususnya dalam binaan dapat tidaknya.
senses.nuances: 这是依句法产生的名词性解释，不是独立的固定名词。词根 dapat 的“能够”义与名词化成分 -nya 共同构成表达；现代说明文也常改写为 sama ada … dapat …。[DBP：-nya 的名词化功能](https://dewanbahasa.jendeladbp.my/2022/03/16/2777/)

etymology.historical_story: Dapatnya is best understood through Malay grammar rather than an invented ancient compound. Dapat supplies meanings involving obtaining or ability, while attached -nya receives its function from the sentence. Malay also uses -nya to turn expressions into noun-like units. This explains why a single written form can require different English or Chinese translations. [DBP grammar discussion](https://dewanbahasa.jendeladbp.my/2022/03/16/2777/)

etymology.historical_story: DBP identifies kendali as Javanese in origin and records its concrete meaning as a bridle or reins. That image provides a useful way to understand its wider Malay uses: guiding a horse, controlling impulses, and managing an organization all involve direction. Dikendalikan presents the entity receiving that direction as the grammatical subject.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 想象 kendali 是手中的缰绳：mengendalikan 是“操控”，加被动 di- 成为 dikendalikan——“被操控、被管理”。

morphology.pattern_note: di- 构成被动形式，词根 tikam 保持不变；此 di- 必须连写。资料包的 Jawi تيکم 是词根拼写，完整 ditikam 为 ديتيکم。音节栏保留资料包的 null，分析可分为 di.ti.kam。

etymology.historical_story: The root tikam belongs to the vocabulary of piercing weapons; dictionary examples include knives and the keris. Adding di- shifts attention from the person wielding the weapon to whoever receives the stab. The same piercing image also supports literary descriptions of cold, sound, and emotional hurt. This is a semantic connection, rather than a claim about the word's earliest origin. See [DBP PRPM](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=202792&keyword=tikam).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: tikam 是“刺”，前面加被动 di- 就是“被刺”；听到 dari belakang，再根据语境判断是否指“背叛”。

senses.ms_definition: Istilah bahasa Inggeris bagi orang yang pekerjaannya menggiring ternakan, khususnya lembu atau biri-biri, dari satu tempat ke tempat lain atau ke pasar.

etymology.historical_story: English drover comes from drove, a noun meaning a herd of animals driven together, plus the agent suffix -er. The occupation involved moving cattle or sheep toward markets. Etymological records place the occupational noun in the early fifteenth century, with earlier surname evidence. Its resemblance to driver reflects their connection with the verb drive. [Drover etymology](https://www.etymonline.com/word/drover)

etymology.historical_story: The root cinta is generally traced to Sanskrit cintā, associated with thought, care and anxiety. Malay developed a prominent meaning of love, while older senses involving sorrow and longing remain in dictionaries. Dicintai adds Malay passive morphology to this inherited vocabulary, placing the beloved person or thing at the centre. See [IIUM discussion](https://irep.iium.edu.my/81688/1/Cinta%20dalam%20islam%20Satu%20Kupasan.pdf).

etymology.historical_story: Capai links physical reaching with reaching a destination, fulfilling an ambition and obtaining results. These dictionary senses provide a memorable image: a hand extends towards something, just as effort extends towards a goal. Dicapai turns attention to what is reached. This is a semantic illustration, rather than a claim about the chronological development of those meanings.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 capai 想成“伸手够到”；加 di- 后，东西被够到，目标被达到：dicapai。

morphology.pattern_note: di- 标记被动，-kan 在此形成使动意义。词根末尾 k 与 -kan 的 k 均保留，写作 kk；di- 是前缀，必须连写。词包的词根标记更正为 naik。

etymology.historical_story: Dinaikkan is a transparent Malay formation built on naik, meaning to go up. Adding -kan makes something rise; di- presents that action from the affected thing's perspective. This upward image connects flags, salaries, ranks and even dough. The connection is grammatical and semantic, rather than evidence of a separate borrowing. [Source: PRPM menaikkan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=72508&keyword=menaikkan).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: naik＝上升，-kan＝使它上升，di-＝从被提升者看动作：dinaikkan 就是“被升高、被提高”。两个 k 来自 naik + kan。

etymology.historical_story: Disember belongs to the international family of month names represented by English December and Latin December. The Latin element decem means ten, preserving an older Roman position even though December is now month twelve. Malay treats Disember as a complete month name; its opening di is unrelated to the Malay passive prefix. [Roman calendar reference](https://latininscriptions.ashmus.ox.ac.uk/resources/resources/AshLI-RomanCalendar-WORKSHEET.pdf)

etymology.historical_story: Disuruh is built transparently from suruh and the passive prefix di-. DBP also records a proverb pairing being instructed with going, and being called with coming, to describe obedience. That cultural association helps explain why the word often evokes errands and duties, although ordinary family requests can be much gentler than military orders.

etymology.historical_story: Deva belongs to the Sanskrit and Pali religious vocabulary and is traditionally explained through the image of a shining or celestial being. Buddhist texts describe devas visiting the Buddha, yet remaining subject to death and rebirth. Malay commonly uses the related form dewa, while deva may be retained when discussing the terminology of particular religious texts. [Buddhist Publication Society](https://accesstoinsight.org/lib/authors/ireland/wheel107.pdf)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 deva 和 dewa 并排记：宗教文本里的 deva，对应熟悉的“神祇／天人”；这是词形联想，不是现代马来语派生公式。

cultural_pragmatics.usage_etiquette: 它不区分男性和女性，翻译应依据上下文选择“他”或“她”。学校作文、公函和正式工作邮件应采用标准拼写 dia；直接引述聊天原文时可以保留 die。

sociolinguistic_register.politeness_note: die 宜限于熟人聊天。正式文字改写为 dia；尊敬地指称长辈、老师或受尊重的人时，可按关系与场合使用 beliau、姓名或职衔。
sociolinguistic_register.usage_etiquette: 它不区分男性和女性，翻译应依据上下文选择“他”或“她”。学校作文、公函和正式工作邮件应采用标准拼写 dia；直接引述聊天原文时可以保留 die。

etymology.historical_story: Die illustrates how conversational pronunciation enters informal writing. The standard pronoun is dia, but speakers may weaken its final vowel, and messages sometimes represent that sound with e. A Malaysian study of SMS language explicitly lists die alongside dia. Its significance is therefore sociolinguistic: an established pronoun receives a casual spelling, rather than becoming a new standard dictionary word.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 看见聊天里的 die，先还原成 dia＝他／她；这里的 e 提醒你听到的是弱化元音，不要按英语 /daɪ/ 去读。

morphology.pattern_note: 现代马来语将其作为完整借词词基，不拆成马来语前后缀。首音节 dé 的 e 为前元音，并非央元音 /ə/。

word_family.gloss: 实行民主；按民主原则行事

senses.zh_definition: 民主政体；由人民直接治理，或通过选举产生的代表治理的政治制度。
senses.en_definition: Government by the people, directly or through elected representatives.
senses.ms_definition: Sistem pemerintahan yang kuasanya dilaksanakan oleh rakyat sendiri atau melalui wakil yang dipilih dalam pilihan raya.
senses.nuances: 最常见的政治义，指治理制度或原则；demokratik 才是通常表示“民主的”的形容词。三个义项及派生词依据 [DBP《Kamus Dewan》词条](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=74812&keyword=demokrasi)，马来语释义在此展开并改写。

senses.zh_definition: 由全体成员共同掌握最终权力的政治或社会组织。
senses.en_definition: A political or social body ultimately controlled by all its members.
senses.ms_definition: Unit politik atau sosial yang pada asasnya berada di bawah kuasa semua anggotanya.
senses.nuances: 指实行成员共同治理的组织或共同体本身，而非仅指制度。实际语篇中常与第一义重叠，须根据所指对象判断。

etymology.historical_story: Demokrasi ultimately belongs to the international vocabulary descended from Greek dēmokratia, combining dēmos, 'people', with kratos, 'power' or 'rule'. These historical components explain the central idea of popular government. In modern Malay, however, the word functions as a complete base, allowing local formations such as berdemokrasi and pendemokrasian rather than Greek-style word building.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 拆义记忆：demo 联想到人民，krasi 联想到治理权；demokrasi 就是人民参与掌握治理权。此拆法用于词源记忆，不是马来语词缀分析。

etymology.historical_story: English diamond travelled through French and Latin from Greek adamas, a name associated with exceptionally hard substances. Its history therefore connects the gemstone with hardness as well as brilliance. In Malaysian Malay, the English spelling belongs to English expressions or language mixing; DBP supplies berlian and intan as the relevant Malay equivalents. [Word history](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/diamond); [Malay equivalents](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=72508&keyword=berlian).

etymology.historical_story: The base jadual names both a timetable and an organized table of information. Malay builds menjadualkan from that noun, then uses dijadualkan when the scheduled event or tabulated material becomes the grammatical subject. The two dictionary meanings preserve this connection between organizing time and organizing facts. [DBP: jadual](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=Jadual)

etymology.historical_story: Ditempatkan shows Malay word formation turning a place into an action. The noun tempat means place; menempatkan means to place or accommodate, and ditempatkan presents the recipient as the grammatical subject. The same spatial idea extends naturally to staff postings and figurative standing. Its structure is Malay morphology, rather than an independently borrowed whole word. Basis: [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?d=175768&keyword=menempatkan).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: tempat 是“地方”；di-...-kan 把视角转向被安排的人或物：被安排到一个地方 → 放置、安置、派驻。

morphology.pattern_note: root_word 按数据包保留，属于未解析占位值；实际词根是 cerita，本词不是词根。di- 标示被动，-kan 构成与 menceritakan 对应的及物动词；词根首音 c 保留。affix_type 按给定枚举记 circumfix，实际可分别分析 di- 与 -kan。数据包 syllables、jawi、root_jawi 均缺失；实际音节可分 di.ce.ri.ta.kan。动词前缀 di- 须连写。

senses.zh_definition: 被讲述、叙述或记述；使故事、经历或事件成为叙述的内容。
senses.en_definition: To be told, narrated, or recounted, as a story, experience, or event.
senses.ms_definition: Dikisahkan atau diriwayatkan oleh seseorang, sama ada secara lisan atau bertulis.
senses.nuances: 这是 menceritakan“讲述”义的被动形式；本马来语释义依据 DBP 词条改写，并非独立条目的逐字引文。di- 不表示过去时：akan diceritakan 为“将被讲述”，telah diceritakan 为“已被讲述”。施事可用 oleh 引出。来源：[DBP：cerita](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=cerita)。

senses.zh_definition: 被告知、透露或传述；指消息、秘密或事情的内容被说给别人听。
senses.en_definition: To be communicated or disclosed to someone, as information, a matter, or a secret.

etymology.historical_story: Cerita is traced to Sanskrit carita, associated with deeds, events, and narrative. Malay builds diceritakan from this established base with passive di- and suffix -kan. The form also fits an enduring cultural practice: stories passed between generations by grandparents and storytellers, with the narrative itself placed at the centre of the sentence. [Etymology](https://repositori.kemendikdasmen.go.id/26597/1/Bernd%20Nothofer_Pengantar%20Etimologi%20lengkap%20pdf.pdf), [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=cerita)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 看到 cerita 就想到“故事”；前面 di- 把镜头转向被讲的内容：cerita itu diceritakan＝那个故事被讲出来。

etymology.historical_story: Daro belongs to Sarawak’s place-name heritage rather than to an established everyday Malay word family. The local council recounts a story connecting the name with Dao Aro, glossed as Bagus Ke. Because the account is explicitly presented as a story, it should be remembered as a local naming tradition rather than a proven linguistic derivation. [Local council account](https://matu-darodc.sarawak.gov.my/web/subpage/webpage_view/113).

etymology.historical_story: Baca is associated with Sanskrit vaca, meaning speaking, in the World Loanword Database’s account of the related form membaca. The connection makes reading aloud an illuminating cultural association, alongside silent reading. Dibaca adds the Malay passive prefix di-, directing attention to the text or other thing being read rather than to its reader. [World Loanword Database](https://wold.clld.org/word/71261839746078626).

etymology.historical_story: Danau belongs to an ancient Austronesian word family reconstructed as *danaw, meaning lake. Related forms occur across languages of Taiwan, the Philippines and island Southeast Asia. Malay preserves this inherited landscape word alongside tasik. The resemblance between Malay danau and forms such as Iban danaw reflects linguistic ancestry rather than a modern borrowing from English. [南岛语比较词典](https://acd.clld.org/cognatesets/30239)

etymology.historical_story: Davis is commonly explained as a patronymic surname associated with David, including the Welsh form Dafydd: historically, it identified someone's relationship to a father bearing that name. A family relationship thus became a hereditary name. In a modern Malay sentence, however, Davis identifies its bearer; it is not translated as a statement about that person's father. [Source: Dictionary of American Family Names](https://www.ancestry.com/last-name-meaning/Davis).

senses.zh_definition: 由某人领导、率领或担任负责人；mengetuai 的被动形式。

etymology.historical_story: Diketuai is a grammatical formation built on ketua, meaning a leader or head. Its story is the productive Malay relationship between active and passive verbs: mengetuai presents the leader as the subject, while diketuai presents the group. This makes it useful for introducing delegations and teams. No separate borrowing history is established here. See [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=mengetuai).

senses.zh_definition: 魔鬼；恶灵。英语 the Devil 常特指宗教中的撒旦。
senses.en_definition: An evil supernatural being; with the, especially Satan.

senses.ms_definition: Secara kiasan dalam bahasa Inggeris, orang yang sangat jahat atau, secara berseloroh, orang yang nakal.

senses.nuances: lucky devil 和 poor devil 中通常没有宗教含义，应按整体语气翻译。[Cambridge Dictionary](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/devil?q=devils)

senses.zh_definition: 用浓烈、辛辣的调味料制作食物。

senses.ms_definition: Dalam bahasa Inggeris, menyediakan makanan dengan perasa yang kuat atau pedas.
senses.nuances: 烹饪义，常以 deviled 或 devilled 出现。devilled eggs 是菜名，具体做法未必很辣。[Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/devil)

etymology.historical_story: English devil continues Old English forms such as deofol. Its history leads through Latin diabolus to Greek diabolos, associated with accusing or slandering. Religious transmission shaped the supernatural meaning, while later everyday usage extended it to wicked people, mischievous children and humorous descriptions. This history concerns English, rather than an established Malay borrowing. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/devil)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 /ˈdev.əl/ 和故事里长角的“魔鬼”形象绑定；遇到 little devil 再切换成“小捣蛋”，避免一律按宗教意义理解。
